title: The complexity of entangled graph colouring via polymorphisms
abstract: Constraint satisfaction problems (CSPs) with operator assignments to the variables provide a well-structured setting to study the decision complexity of the entangled value of classes of nonlocal games. Due to the CSP dichotomy theorem, the complexity of constraint satisfaction problems with classical assignments can be fully understood by studying the symmetries of the CSP, in terms of the polymorphisms of the underlying relational structure. In this work, we show that the polymorphism-based reductions between CSPs can be generalised to gap-preserving reductions between entangled CSPs based on an entangled analogue of the polymorphisms. This reduction allows us to show undecidability of entangled graph colouring with more than three colours, a problem that has proved resistant to prior hardness reductions based on commutativity gadgets.
summary: This theoretical paper develops advanced algebraic techniques to analyze the computational complexity of quantum constraint satisfaction problems, particularly entangled graph colouring. By generalizing polymorphism-based reductions, the authors prove that this problem is RE-complete for n >= 3. This work advances the understanding of quantum complexity by providing tools for hardness proofs in settings lacking simple classical gadgets.
main_problem: The paper studies the decision complexity of entangled value classes of nonlocal games, specifically focusing on entangled graph colouring.
main_result: It proves that gapped non-oracular entangled n-colouring for all n >= 3 is RE-complete, extending hardness results beyond those relying on commutativity gadgets.
method: The authors generalize polymorphism-based reductions from classical CSPs to 'gap-preserving reductions' for entangled CSPs using an 'entangled analogue of the polymorphisms.'
model_or_system: The model involves nonlocal games derived from Constraint Satisfaction Problems (CSPs) analyzed using $C^*$-algebras to describe quantum operator assignments (tensor product or commuting-operator model).
key_observables: The gap between success probabilities for yes/no instances (gapped vs. gapless CSPs) and the complexity class (RE-complete).
important_parameters: The number of colors (n), the distinction between oracular and non-oracular settings, and the structure of the underlying relational algebra.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on developing algebraic structures like 'minions' and their duals, 'cominions,' to establish the necessary reduction machinery.
paper_structure: The paper builds from classical CSP complexity theory (Schaefer's dichotomy) to introduce entangled CSPs using $C^*$-algebras. It develops the machinery of cominion homomorphisms to generalize reductions, culminating in the proof of RE-completeness for entangled graph colouring.
why_interesting: It provides a powerful, general algebraic framework to establish computational hardness results for quantum constraint satisfaction problems, which is crucial for understanding the limits of quantum correlation in computation.
